summary: Hendricks Head Light on the Sheepscot River: lit in 1829, the square brick tower of 1875, discontinued in 1933, privately owned and closed to the public.

access.note: Privately owned and not open to the public; the grounds, dwelling and tower are closed. The tower can be seen from West Southport Beach.

events.note: First light (John Upham, 1 December 1829); station built with a rubble stone cottage and polygonal tower.
LighthouseFriends dates a fifth-order Fresnel lens to 1857 (changing the light to a white flash). The USLHS record gives 1875 for its original lens. Unresolved.
Square brick tower and frame keeper's house replaced the 1829 station.
Fifth-order Fresnel lens (USLHS 'Year Original Lens Installed: 1875').
Bell struck by machinery, in operation 15 July 1891 (Lighthouse Board).
Schooner Leader struck Green Island near Southport after mistaking the light for Burnt Island (LighthouseFriends, citing an October 1879 newspaper).
Couple in a rowboat rescued after the fog bell was rung on the keeper's alarm (LighthouseFriends).
Discontinued 16 October 1933 as a cost-saving measure after a lighted buoy was set nearby.
Sold to the Browne family; the nomination and LighthouseFriends name the buyers differently.
Coast Guard recommissioned and automated the light.
January 1978 winter storm destroyed the boathouse and the walkway to the bell tower.
Fifth-order lens removed in favour of a modern optic (LighthouseFriends).
Browne family sold the station to private owners.

corrections.why: The standing tower is square (NRHP: 'square tapered brick'; USLHS: 'Tower Shape: SQUARE'; LighthouseFriends: 'square'). The record's conical_masonry describes no surviving structure here.
The present brick tower was built in 1875 (NRHP; USLHS 'Year Tower Established: 1875'). The 1829 structure was a stone cottage with a polygonal tower, replaced in 1875.
The 1975 entries come from Wikidata. The nomination and LighthouseFriends show the light discontinued in 1933, then recommissioned and automated by the Coast Guard in 1951.
Same error as the 1975 event: the automation followed the Coast Guard's recommissioning in 1951 (NRHP; LighthouseFriends).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's first-year conflict is the 1829 first light against Wikidata's 1975 first lighting. The 1975 date belongs to the later recommissioning (1951 per the nomination and LighthouseFriends), not to the first lighting.

notes_for_editor: Lens: LighthouseFriends dates a fifth-order lens to 1857 (fixed to flashing); the USLHS record gives 1875 for its original lens. Tower height: 40 ft (LighthouseFriends) against 39 ft (USLHS). Tower shape: the record's Wikidata 'conical_masonry' is contradicted by NRHP, USLHS and LighthouseFriends (square). Buyers in 1935: the nomination says 'W. Prichard and Mary L. Browne' (OCR; check the page image), LighthouseFriends 'Dr. William P. Browne of Connecticut'; the buyer's name is printed as the sources print it. Jaruel Marr's service: 28 years (Kennebec Journal 1907) against 29 (LighthouseFriends' logbook quote; the USLHS roster 1866-1895). LighthouseFriends prints the logbook entry with the year 1855; the story omits the year. The 1875 Lighthouse Board quotation comes from LighthouseFriends; the original 1875 report is not in the corpus. The baby-in-a-box story is LighthouseFriends' retelling of Snow (1945) and is disputed; no first-hand record was located. The 1879 Leader wreck and the 1932 Shep rescue come from LighthouseFriends only (its sources include Lighthouse Digest, not read). The NRHP statement of significance reads 'early 1970s' in the OCR, which must be an OCR error for 1870s; not quoted. The Browne-family and later owners are not named beyond the published names. Wolcott Marr's service at the Cuckolds and Cape Elizabeth has no dates in the sources and is not linked as other_stations. The 1922 Commissioner quote is OCR'd ('motor l>oat'), quoted only up to 'motor'. Not used: the 1891 Republican Journal and 1904 Portland Press hits, which mention Hendricks Head in lists or ads only. Fact-check 2026-10-22: the 40 ft (LighthouseFriends) against 39 ft (USLHS) tower height is now stated in the text. The LighthouseFriends logbook entry is dated "July 1, 1855" in its text; the relief it records was in 1895 (Jaruel Marr 1866-1895 in the roster), so 1855 is taken as a typo and no year is given in the story. The 1935 buyer names from the NRHP ("W. Prichard and Mary L. Browne") are OCR text not checked against the page image. The NRHP "tapered bell that was built in 1890" is OCR and is read as the bell tower.
